entries.originalText: The Voice of the Disciple
entries.modernizedText: The Voice of the Disciple

entries.originalText: O Lord my God, prevent Thou Thy servant with the blessings of Thy sweetness, that I may be enabled to draw near worthily and devoutly to Thy glorious Sacrament.
entries.modernizedText: O Lord my God, go before Your servant with the blessings of Your sweetness, so that I may be enabled to draw near worthily and devoutly to Your glorious Sacrament.

entries.originalText: Awaken my heart towards Thee, and deliver me from heavy slumber.
entries.modernizedText: Awaken my heart toward You and deliver me from heavy sleep.

entries.originalText: Visit me with Thy salvation that I may in spirit taste Thy sweetness, which plentifully lieth hid in this Sacrament as in a fountain.
entries.modernizedText: Visit me with Your salvation, so that in spirit I may taste Your sweetness, which lies abundantly hidden in this Sacrament as in a fountain.

entries.originalText: Lighten also mine eyes to behold this so great mystery, and strengthen me that I may believe it with undoubting faith.
entries.modernizedText: Enlighten my eyes also to behold this great mystery, and strengthen me to believe it with undoubting faith.

entries.originalText: For it is Thy word, not human power; it is Thy holy institution, not the invention of man.
entries.modernizedText: For it is Your word, not human power; it is Your holy institution, not a human invention.

entries.originalText: For no man is found fit in himself to receive and to understand these things, which transcend even the wisdom of the Angels.
entries.modernizedText: For no one is found fit in himself to receive and understand these things, which transcend even the wisdom of the Angels.

entries.originalText: What portion then shall I, unworthy sinner, who am but dust and ashes, be able to search into and comprehend of so deep a Sacrament?
entries.modernizedText: What part of so deep a Sacrament shall I, an unworthy sinner who am only dust and ashes, be able to search into and comprehend?

entries.originalText: O Lord, in the simplicity of my heart, in good and firm faith, and according to Thy will, I draw nigh unto Thee with hope and reverence, and truly believe that Thou art here present in the Sacrament, God and man.
entries.modernizedText: O Lord, in simplicity of heart, in good and firm faith, and according to Your will, I draw near to You with hope and reverence, and truly believe that You are here present in the Sacrament, God and man.

entries.originalText: Thou willest therefore that I receive Thee and unite myself to Thee in charity.
entries.modernizedText: You will, therefore, that I receive You and unite myself to You in charity.

entries.originalText: Wherefore I beseech Thy mercy, and implore Thee to give me Thy special grace, to this end, that I may be wholly dissolved and overflow with love towards Thee, and no more suffer any other consolation to enter into me.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore I beg Your mercy and implore You to give me Your special grace, so that I may be wholly dissolved and overflow with love toward You, and allow no other consolation to enter me.

entries.originalText: For this most high and most glorious Sacrament is the health of the soul and the body, the medicine of all spiritual sickness, whereby I am healed of my sins, my passions are bridled, temptations are conquered or weakened, more grace is poured into me, virtue begun is increased, faith is made firm, hope is strengthened, and charity is enkindled and enlarged.
entries.modernizedText: For this most high and glorious Sacrament is the health of soul and body, the medicine for all spiritual sickness, by which I am healed of my sins, my passions are restrained, temptations are conquered or weakened, more grace is poured into me, virtue already begun is increased, faith is made firm, hope is strengthened, and charity is kindled and enlarged.

entries.originalText: For in this Sacrament Thou hast bestowed many good things and still bestowest them continually on Thine elect who communicate devoutly, O my God, Lifter up of my soul, Repairer of human infirmity, and Giver of all inward consolation.
entries.modernizedText: For in this Sacrament You have bestowed many good things and still bestow them continually on Your elect who communicate devoutly, O my God, Lifter up of my soul, Restorer of human weakness, and Giver of all inward consolation.

entries.originalText: For Thou pourest into them much consolation against all sorts of tribulation, and out of the deep of their own misery Thou liftest them up to the hope of Thy protection, and with ever new grace, dost inwardly refresh and enlighten them; so that they who felt themselves to be anxious and without affection before Communion, afterwards being refreshed with heavenly food and drink, find themselves changed for the better.
entries.modernizedText: For You pour much consolation into them against all kinds of trouble, and out of the depths of their own misery You lift them to the hope of Your protection. With ever new grace You inwardly refresh and enlighten them, so that those who felt anxious and without affection before Communion afterwards, refreshed with heavenly food and drink, find themselves changed for the better.

entries.originalText: And even in such wise Thou dealest severally with Thine elect, that they may truly acknowledge and clearly make proof that they have nothing whatsoever of their own, and what goodness and grace come to them from Thee; because being in themselves cold, hard of heart, indevout, through Thee they become fervent, zealous, and devout.
entries.modernizedText: And You deal with each of Your elect in this way, so that they may truly acknowledge and clearly experience that they have nothing at all of their own, and that whatever goodness and grace they have comes from You; for though in themselves cold, hard of heart, and lacking devotion, through You they become fervent, zealous, and devout.

entries.originalText: For who is there coming humbly to the fountain of sweetness, carrieth not away thence at the least some little of that sweetness?
entries.modernizedText: For who comes humbly to the fountain of sweetness and does not carry away at least a little of that sweetness?

entries.originalText: Or who standing by a large fire, feeleth not from thence a little of its heat?
entries.modernizedText: Or who stands by a large fire and does not feel a little of its heat?

entries.originalText: And Thou art ever a full and overflowing fountain, a fire continually burning, and never going out.
entries.modernizedText: And You are always a full and overflowing fountain, a fire continually burning and never going out.

entries.originalText: Wherefore if it is not suffered to me to draw from the fulness of the fountain, nor to drink unto satisfying, yet will I set my lips to the mouth of the heavenly conduit, that at least I may receive a small drop to quench my thirst, that I dry not up within my heart.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore, if I am not permitted to draw from the fullness of the fountain or drink until satisfied, I will still set my lips to the mouth of the heavenly channel, so that I may receive at least a small drop to quench my thirst and not dry up within my heart.

entries.originalText: And if I am not yet able to be altogether heavenly and so enkindled as the Cherubim and Seraphim, yet will I endeavour to give myself unto devotion, and to prepare my heart, that I may gain if it be but a little flame of the divine fire, through the humble receiving of the life-giving Sacrament.
entries.modernizedText: And if I am not yet able to be altogether heavenly and as kindled as the Cherubim and Seraphim, I will still endeavor to give myself to devotion and prepare my heart, so that through humble reception of the life-giving Sacrament I may gain, if only a little, a flame of the divine fire.

entries.originalText: But whatsoever is wanting unto me, O merciful Jesus, Most Holy Saviour, do Thou of Thy kindness and grace supply, who hast vouchsafed to call all unto Thee, saying, Come unto me, all ye that are weary and heavy laden, and I will refresh you.
entries.modernizedText: But whatever is lacking in me, O merciful Jesus, Most Holy Savior, supply in Your kindness and grace, You who have graciously called all to You, saying, Come to me, all you who are weary and heavy laden, and I will refresh you.

entries.originalText: I indeed labour in the sweat of my face, I am tormented with sorrow of heart, I am burdened with sins, I am disquieted with temptations, I am entangled and oppressed with many passions, and there is none to help me, there is none to deliver and ease me, but Thou, O Lord God, my Saviour, to whom I commit myself and all things that are mine, that Thou mayest preserve me and lead me unto life eternal.
entries.modernizedText: I indeed labor in the sweat of my face, am tormented with sorrow of heart, burdened with sins, troubled by temptations, entangled and oppressed by many passions; and there is no one to help me, no one to deliver and ease me, but You, O Lord God, my Savior. To You I entrust myself and all that is mine, that You may preserve me and lead me to eternal life.

entries.originalText: Receive me unto the praise and glory of Thy name, who hast prepared Thy Body and Blood to be my meat and drink.
entries.modernizedText: Receive me to the praise and glory of Your name, You who have prepared Your Body and Blood to be my food and drink.

entries.originalText: Grant, O Lord God my Saviour, that with coming often to Thy mysteries the zeal of my devotion may increase.
entries.modernizedText: Grant, O Lord God my Savior, that by coming often to Your mysteries the zeal of my devotion may increase.
